text:
maya: Quick sync — I'm drafting an "entry gateway" checklist for model onboarding that can adapt based on SLA tier & model profile. want feedback on scope and runtime boundaries.
ben: +1. do you mean adaptive checks that skip heavy benches for tiny models?
kai: yep. idea: classify model by cost/latency/size -> pick a smoke suite. avoids running full bench for every PR.
sophia: important: we need deterministic signal for rollout decisions. lightweight probes must map to canary metrics otherwise noisy.
maya: proposed coarse buckets: tiny (<1B params), small (1–7B), medium (7–70B), large (70B+). each bucket has default probe set.
elena: question: where do we draw the line between "onboard" responsibilities and runtime admission? e.g., KV cache correctness — is that an onboarding check or a runtime thing?
ben: I think basic KV cache sanity (prefix caching works, no corruption) should be onboarding smoke. production runtime covers ongoing cache eviction behavior under load.
kai: agree. also: compatibility checks must include shape + dtype + attention mask semantics. small models can pass faster via binary compatibility shim but we should flag shims in metadata.
sophia: suggestion: encode adaptivity rules as a single config blob used by intake and gatekeeper. sample config:```yaml
buckets:
  tiny:
    probes: [latency_smoke, basic_safety, decode_consistency]
    max_wall_time: 10m
  large:
    probes: [latency_smoke, full_microbench, eval_sample_regressions]
    max_wall_time: 2h
policies:
  allow_shim: true
  ramp_to_dedicated_if_latency>300ms: true
```
maya: nice. also want to tie max_wall_time to SLA tier: free -> short, enterprise -> allow longer benches.
elena: what about cost accounting? running full microbench for large models is expensive — we should deduct from team credits or require approval.
ben: add a preflight approval signal if estimated GPU-minutes > X. we already have an approvals bot; tie into that.
deploy-bot: estimate for model "llama2-78b-quant" = 420 GPU-minutes for full_microbench. approval required.
kai: fallback behavior: if a model times out on the heavy bench, do we allow partial admission (canary with limited qps) or reject outright?
sophia: prefer graded admission: fail-open for non-security issues with automatic low-qps canary + telemetry gating. fail-closed for safety or API-contract breakage errors.
maya: need deterministic gating signals: list of required gates that must pass for full admission: compile_success, decode_consistency(<1% diff on golden), safety_no_hits, basic_latency(< target_by_tier). everything else can be advisory.
elena: compatibility metadata must include: runtime ABI version, quantization type, supported sequence lengths, kv-cache-behavior, shim_applied(boolean). that helps runtime router pick fallbacks.
ben: interface boundary note: onboarding must emit a machine-readable "admit_token" with metadata and provenances (bench artifacts, git commit, seed). runtime can refuse tokens older than N days or when model has incompatible runtime flags.
kai: also track reproducibility: hash of model weights + export config + random_seed used for smoke. store in registry artifact.
sophia: ops question: how do we surface bench regressions over time? we need temporal baselines and a small set of golden inputs per bucket.
maya: yes — keep golden set per bucket and per domain (chat/completion/embedding). bench must produce deterministic metrics on the golden set. if variance > threshold, flag for manual review.
ben: small nit: golden inputs should avoid copyrighted content — use synthetic + sanitized real traces.
elena: rollout playbook: onboarding -> canary(qps 1% for 24h)-> gradual ramp (5%, 20%, 100%) with automatic rollback on metric breach. metrics: p50/p95 latency, error-rate, safety hits, model-quality delta on golden set.
kai: implement canary throttle via routing tags emitted by admit_token. runtime router uses tags to select weight.
maya: one more tradeoff: depth of bench vs wall time. We should expose a "fast-entry" mode for experiments that runs only essential checks and tags model as experimental with explicit warnings in registry.
sophia: agree. label schema: [admit: {level: full|experimental|restricted}, reasons: [...]] as part of registry entry.
ben: blockers: we need infra to run microbench on both accel types (A100 vs H100) because perf differs. bench results must be labeled by hw type.
elena: security: ensure checksum verification of artifacts and ephemeral creds for bench runs. also audit logs for who triggered heavy benches.
kai: action items: 1) maya draft config schema for adaptive gateway (eta wed). 2) ben to stub admit_token format + examples. 3) sophia to assemble golden-inputs per bucket. 4) elena to prototype approval gating with deploy-bot.
maya: thanks — I'll post a follow-up RFC with config examples and admit_token proto. anyone want to add items?
sophia: add: integration test for shim detection (should fail admission if shim unsupported in target runtime).
ben: I'll add a sample admit_token:```json
{"model":"llama2-70b","hash":"sha256:...","admit":{"level":"experimental","buckets":["large"]},"benchings":[{"name":"latency_smoke","result":"pass","hw":"A100", "run_id":"r123"}]}
```
maya: perfect. ok closing thread, i'll put RFC up by wed EOD. :thumbsup:
